title: Small-etale comparison calculus on algebraic-space tests of a stack
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Algebraic spaces and their small etale sites are [def-trf-algebraic-space]; quasi-coherent modules on them are [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], module sheaves are [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and all pullbacks below are tensor pullbacks [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Let $\mathcal Z/S$ be an algebraic stack [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack] with big fppf site and structure sheaf [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra], and let $H$ be a module sheaf there. For a map $z:V\to\mathcal Z$ from an algebraic space, let $H_z$ be its small-etale restriction: on an etale scheme $T\to V$ it has value $H(z|_T)$. For $a:V\to W$ and a two-isomorphism $\theta:z\Rightarrow w\circ a$, restriction induces a natural comparison $c_{a,\theta}:a^*H_w\to H_z$. These comparisons are natural in $H$, are identities for identity arrows, respect composition of arrows and their two-isomorphisms, and agree with restriction on etale scheme charts. In particular, for composable arrows $a:V\to W$, $b:W\to B$ with the prescribed two-isomorphisms, $$c_{ba}=c_a\circ a^*c_b$$ under $(ba)^*\cong a^*b^*$. They are isomorphisms if $a$ is etale. If every scheme-test restriction of $H$ is the associated etale sheaf of a quasi-coherent Zariski module [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-pbc-etale-site], then every $H_z$ is quasi-coherent on $V_{\mathrm{et}}$. If, in addition, the scheme-test comparisons are isomorphisms for flat scheme maps [def-weil-flat-morphism], then $c_{a,\theta}$ is an isomorphism for every flat algebraic-space map $a$ [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. These assertions also apply to the canonical two-isomorphisms between maps coming from a groupoid presentation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-fibred-fppf-space-module-comparisons] to the underlying category fibred in groupoids of $\mathcal Z$, its given fppf module $H$, and its algebraic-space tests. Its restriction formula is exactly $H_z(T)=H(z|_T)$, and its adjoint comparison gives $c_{a,\theta}$. Its naturality, identity, composition and scheme-test clauses give the stated coherence and agreement on charts, including the displayed formula with the pasted two-isomorphism. Its etale clause gives invertibility for etale $a$. Only the clauses for arbitrary modules are used here; $H$ need not be quasi-coherent on the big site.

proof.text: Assume the scheme-test quasi-coherence hypothesis. For every etale scheme chart $e:E\to V$, the etale comparison identifies $e^*H_z$ with $H_{ze}$. Etale pullback is restriction to the localized site by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. By hypothesis $H_{ze}$ is associated to a quasi-coherent Zariski module, so [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] says it has local free presentations on $E_{\mathrm{et}}$. Each etale cover and presentation on that slice is also a cover and presentation over the corresponding object of $V_{\mathrm{et}}$. Thus every object of $V_{\mathrm{et}}$ has a covering with the presentations required by [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and $H_z$ is quasi-coherent. This uses local quasi-coherence only, not quasi-coherence of $H$ on the big site.

Now let $a:V\to W$ be flat. Choose surjective etale scheme atlases $e:E\to V$ and $t:T\to W$. Set $P=E\times_W T$, with $d:P\to E$ and $f:P\to T$. This is a scheme by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. The base-change covering assertion of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] says $d$ is surjective etale, and composition gives a surjective etale scheme chart $r=ed:P\to V$. We have $ar=tf$. Both $r$ and $t$ are etale scheme charts; hence the chart definition of flatness in [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] says that the scheme map $f$ is flat. This construction does not require $a$ to be representable by schemes.

source.place: Tag 0762 (definition-flat-base-change), extension to algebraic-space tests by scheme atlases; scheme fibre products over algebraic spaces.

proof.text: Equip $z r$ and $w t$ with the two-isomorphism over $f$ obtained from $\theta$ and $ar=tf$. Apply the comparison composition law twice. Under the canonical tensor-pullback identifications it gives $$c_r\circ r^*c_{a,\theta}=c_f\circ f^*c_t:r^*a^*H_w\longrightarrow H_{zr}.$$ Here $c_r$ and $c_t$ are invertible because $r,t$ are etale, and $c_f$ is invertible by the assumed flat scheme-test property since $P,T$ are schemes and $f$ is flat. Functors preserve inverse pairs, so $f^*c_t$ is invertible. Therefore $r^*c_{a,\theta}=c_r^{-1}c_f f^*c_t$ is invertible. By [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction], $r^*$ is ordinary restriction to $P_{\mathrm{et}}$. To descend this isomorphism, for each etale scheme $A\to V$ use its surjective etale scheme cover $A\times_VP\to A$. The locally defined inverses agree on overlaps: each is an inverse of the same restricted morphism, and inverses are unique. The sheaf gluing axiom glues their values on every target section, giving a module map inverse on $A$; uniqueness makes these inverses commute with restriction in $A$. Consequently $c_{a,\theta}$ is an isomorphism on $V_{\mathrm{et}}$.

source.place: Tags 075D and 076R (comparison composition); stacks-cohomology.tex Tag 0762 (definition-flat-base-change); etale sheaf gluing.

proof.text: For maps supplied by a groupoid presentation, take the canonical two-isomorphisms as the two-isomorphisms of tests in the preceding construction. The naturality and pasted-composition clause of [lem-sfb-fibred-fppf-space-module-comparisons] applies to these very two-isomorphisms, so it gives the same identity, composition and chart formulas. The quasi-coherence and flat invertibility conclusions already proved apply whenever their respective hypotheses hold. No flatness assumption is asserted for an arbitrary presentation map.
